description: Open Space Toolkit (OSTk) Astrodynamics is an open-source C++ library with Python bindings for orbit, attitude, access and mission analysis, part of the wider Open Space Toolkit. It propagates trajectories with models such as SGP4 from two-line elements and supports access and mission analysis between spacecraft and ground targets, fetching JPL ephemerides and Earth orientation and leap second data from IERS on first use. It covers any Earth orbit scenario defined by the user. It is developed in the open by the Open Space Collective on GitHub with continuous integration and documentation, released as C++ runtime, headers and Python packages and ready-made Docker and JupyterLab containers; version 17.15.0 was published on PyPI on 1 September 2026 under the Apache 2.0 licence. It is free to use. Caveats: the first run needs internet access to fetch reference data, and the library is aimed at developers, not end users. It supports hazard exposure and resilience analysis of satellite constellations and ground segment access, and optimisation of operations; a related record is the Orekit space flight dynamics library.
